workhorse-new
  Write a standalone workflow distribution that loops an agent until a check command exits 0.
  runs: workhorse-new {name} --check {check} --into {into}
  body: NewArgs
  0 → lines of text: the distribution is written under the name and the next steps are printed
  1 → Stderr: the name is not kebab-case, the check is blank, or the target already exists
  2 → Stderr: the name or --check is missing, and the usage is printed
  carries: RunNew
    refuses 2 'usage: workhorse-new [-h] --check CHECK [--into DIR] name\nworkhorse-new: error: the following arguments are required: name, --check'
    refuses 2 'usage: workhorse-new [-h] --check CHECK [--into DIR] name\nworkhorse-new: error: the following arguments are required: name'
    refuses 2 'usage: workhorse-new [-h] --check CHECK [--into DIR] name\nworkhorse-new: error: the following arguments are required: --check'
    refuses 1 "error: '{name}' is not a workflow name: use lowercase letters, digits and single dashes, starting with a letter"
      why: the name becomes the command workhorse-NAME and the python package, so it is a kebab-case word.
    refuses 1 'error: --check is empty: give the shell command that decides when the work is done'
    refuses 1 'error: {target} already exists; pick another name or remove it'
      why: scaffolding never overwrites a distribution a person may have edited.

python -m workhorse_workflows.research.scaffold.new_program
  Write the folder of a research program: its manifest, README, progress log and first gate.
  runs: python -m workhorse_workflows.research.scaffold.new_program --dir {dir} --code-root {code_root} --gate {gate} [--set-default] [--force]
  body: NewProgramArgs
  0 → lines of text (not compared: lines starting '  created '): each file written is named, and the program's findings folder when it is new
  1 → Stderr: the program's manifest is already there and --force was not given
  2 → Stderr: the folder or the source folder is missing, and the usage is printed
  carries: RunNewProgram
    refuses 2 'usage: new_program.py [-h] [--repo REPO] --dir DIR --code-root CODE_ROOT\n                      [--name NAME] [--gate GATE] [--progress PROGRESS]\n                      [--result-branch RESULT_BRANCH] [--ram-gb RAM_GB]\n                      [--cpus CPUS] [--gpu GPU] [--disk-gb DISK_GB]\n                      [--min-containment {premium,best_effort,advisory}]\n                      [--set-default] [--force]\nnew_program.py: error: the following arguments are required: --dir, --code-root'
    refuses 2 'usage: new_program.py [-h] [--repo REPO] --dir DIR --code-root CODE_ROOT\n                      [--name NAME] [--gate GATE] [--progress PROGRESS]\n                      [--result-branch RESULT_BRANCH] [--ram-gb RAM_GB]\n                      [--cpus CPUS] [--gpu GPU] [--disk-gb DISK_GB]\n                      [--min-containment {premium,best_effort,advisory}]\n                      [--set-default] [--force]\nnew_program.py: error: the following arguments are required: --dir'
    refuses 2 'usage: new_program.py [-h] [--repo REPO] --dir DIR --code-root CODE_ROOT\n                      [--name NAME] [--gate GATE] [--progress PROGRESS]\n                      [--result-branch RESULT_BRANCH] [--ram-gb RAM_GB]\n                      [--cpus CPUS] [--gpu GPU] [--disk-gb DISK_GB]\n                      [--min-containment {premium,best_effort,advisory}]\n                      [--set-default] [--force]\nnew_program.py: error: the following arguments are required: --code-root'
    refuses 1 '[new_program] scaffolding {program_dir} (repo=<sandbox>)\n[new_program] refusing to overwrite <sandbox>/{program_dir}/program.yml (pass --force)'
      why: a program folder holds a ledger a person fills in, so the scaffolder stops at the first file it would replace.

AuthorAWorkflow
A person scaffolds a workflow of their own with workhorse-new. The distribution lands in the working
    directory with the check written into its README and workflow. Asking for the same name again is refused and
    leaves what is there alone. The same name into another directory, with another check, is a second distribution.

ScaffoldAResearchProgram
A person stamps a research program folder before running the research workflow. The folder holds the manifest,
    the README, the progress log and the first gate. Stamping it again is refused and leaves the files alone. With
    --force, another first gate and --set-default the files are written again, a second gate file sits beside the
    first, and the active program is pointed at the folder. A missing folder or source folder stops at the usage line.

TryTheWorkflows
A person checks every workflow in a fresh repository before using it. The loop-runner, research, author and
    review-debt and coder dry runs pass. The okf-book dry run is refused until the skill its prompt names is
    installed, and passes once it is. A dry run repeated writes the same run directory again.

WrongTurns\nA person mistypes workhorse-new. A name with capital letters is refused with the rule for names, a blank check\n    is refused, and a missing name or check stops at the usage line. Nothing is written by any of them.
- **bare**: the directory holds nothing. Reached by: a fresh service, nothing done.
- **skills installed**: the skills the prompts name are installed in the repository. Reached by: InstallSkills.
- **scaffolded**: workhorse-new wrote fix-tests here. Reached by: workhorse-new fix-tests --check 'pytest -q'.
- **program written**: a research program folder is written here. Reached by: python -m workhorse_workflows.research.scaffold.new_program --dir specs/demo --code-root src/demo.
- **scaffolded with skills**: fix-tests is written and the skills are installed. Reached by: workhorse-new fix-tests --check 'pytest -q'; InstallSkills.

sources: workflows/src/workhorse_workflows/coder/main/flow.py::Coder, workflows/src/workhorse_workflows/coder/shared/owner.py::cut_notes
Every owner turn and every resolver turn of the coder runs for at most `turn_minutes` minutes, 60 unless the launch
says otherwise. The same value is the turn's pacing advice and its wall-clock deadline. The prompt tells the turn its
minutes, and the run cuts it at that mark.
A turn that is cut keeps its conversation, and the lane asks the operator how to go on. It never goes to the resolver,
because the resolver turn has the same allowance and would cost another hour on the same question. The operator's answer
starts the turn again on the same conversation, with the answer in hand. A merge turn that is cut asks the operator
without commenting on the pull request, because a cut is the allowance running out and not a refused merge.
`turn_minutes` must be a whole number above zero. A launch that gives any other value is refused before any turn starts,
and it names `turn_minutes`. A run resumed from a checkpoint that predates the parameter takes the default of 60.

A review finding can concern a file of the story's spec folder, such as its plan or a recorded measurement. In a workspace whose spec folder sits outside the code repositories, no commit carries that fix.

A fixed answer may therefore cite the spec file by a `- path:` line. The check accepts it when the file exists inside the story's spec folder. The path may be absolute, relative to the spec folder, or end with the folder's own trailing parts. A path that escapes the folder, names a directory or names a missing file does not hold.
Commit evidence and test evidence keep their rules.

A recorded pass with no finding is replayed without the seat, because its calls are the exam after a developer fix.

A recorded finding is never replayed. A replay cannot tell a fixed defect from a standing one, because the defect is declared known in the book and the replay stays green either way. It sent the same finding back to the developer on every visit.
The seat judges each earlier finding again against the running app. The record is rewritten from what it reports, so a finding the app now meets leaves the record and one it still fails stays.

elements: New, DryRunLoopRunner, DryRunResearch, DryRunAuthor, DryRunCoder, DryRunOkfBook, DryRunReviewDebt
Every workhorse-<name> binary is the engine's own command line with one workflow loaded, and its run, dot,
control, inbox, replay and version subcommands start an agent, read a run's recorded state or print the engine's
version. A real run needs an agent CLI and spends money, and the engine's subcommands are the engine's, so the
book plays the two things the workflows package decides by itself: workhorse-new, which writes files, and the
run --dry-run of each workflow, which loads the workflow, stubs every agent turn and node, and writes a run
directory. Sub-flows run standalone (a flow name after run), params, resume and worktree flags are the engine's
and are not played. A dry run ignores --run-id, so every dry run is named <workflow>-dry-run.
Every dry run starts the workflow's whole package and the shared kit it imports, so each dry run names the workflow's
files and the kit's in its source. The sub-flows and the agent prompts of a workflow are read when its run loads, and
a run of one is the engine's.

sources: workflows/src/workhorse_workflows/coder/shared/queue.py::resolve_launch, workflows/src/workhorse_workflows/author/finalize/nodes/artifacts.py::validate_artifacts
A coder launch over every epic, `epic=all` and the default, files the open stories of every epic the project's
milestones list. The epics come in milestone order: a milestone's `dependsOn` milestones first, then its `epics:` list
in order. A superseded milestone gives none. The run files those stories on its own worklist and tracks what it
finished there. It never writes the milestones.
There is no shared epics queue. The coder reads no `index.md` on the epics shelf and no `epics-todo.json`, and keeps no
fallback for either. A run used to remove each finished epic from the shared queue and commit that change, so one run's
progress changed what the next run and every person saw. A person now decides what gets worked by editing the
milestones.
A launch over every epic fails before any turn when no milestone lists an epic, or when a milestone lists an epic the
book does not hold. Author's last check judges what it wrote against the same list, so an Author run that ends green
leaves the coder something to run.

A story's change is its own commits plus the uncommitted work, when a commit carries its trailer.
It is the range from the base when no commit carries it, or when the story's commits are the whole range.
The range is then the same change, read exactly.
The checks, the selection, the covered books, the clone check, the sentinel gate and the stamp all read it this way.
On a shared trunk, the range ran four services' gates for a one-service story.
It also made the seat write book pointers for code other stories wrote.
The stamp writes no verified commit while other commits leave code unnamed.

elements: DryRunCoder, DryRunOkfBook, InstallSkills
The okf-book workflow has four prompts that name a skill (ostler-book): the python book writer, the screen
skeleton and screen reason writers and the catch-up writer. The coder workflow names a skill only
behind a check that the skill is installed, so its dry run passes without one.

The QA of a story a service book covers has four steps. The selection matches the story's diff against the book. The
stack copy comes up. The workflow plays what the selection picked. Then the end review, one agent turn, reads what
the plays left.
The review runs once, after every play passed and before the books are stamped verified. It reads the story's
acceptance criteria, functional and non-functional, numbered by the workflow. It reads `qa-plan.md`, the play
reports, the earlier evidence in the spec folder with its date and commit, and the repository's own tests. It also
reads the claims the book could not state. It may run one bounded check per item, never a whole dataset, a whole
book or production.
Each criterion gets one verdict: played, tested, recorded, checked, unobserved or unmet. Only unmet returns the story
to its developer, and then no book is stamped. Unobserved passes the story, and the workflow records it in
`qa-review.md` and `book-qa.json` for an operator to read. A review that gives no verdict for a criterion gets one
more turn, then the operator is asked.
The review has `review_minutes`, 20 unless the launch says otherwise. A review cut at that mark keeps its
conversation, and the lane asks the operator.
The coder enters the scenario QA only when no service of the story has an executable book. A story whose books
judged it goes from the review to the commit, and a leftover after it is proven again by the books.

A rule above any one service lives in a page of the product book (`product/<slug>.md` beside `services/`), the team book (`teams/<team>/<slug>.md` in the artifacts dir) or the company book (`company/<slug>.md` in the artifacts dir), and the coder's turns read them before they judge or write. The spec turn and the dev turns run `ostler book pages` and read every page it lists, because they cannot list the team and company folders by path, and they use its words. The book turn, the end review and the resolver run `ostler book search` once for each main noun of the story with `--kind company`, `--kind team`, `--kind product` and `--kind decision`. The order of authority is company, team, product, service decision, story. A criterion that contradicts a page is reported as such, never silently judged, and a conflict between two levels is reported and never settled by the agent.

The operator's resolver treats the pages and the decisions as standing decisions, ahead of the story. A question a page settles is not escalated and is not decided against the page. When the operator's answer states a rule that outlives the story, the resolver writes it as a product page in the same turn, with `sources: operator` and the date. The resolver never writes a team or a company page. When the answer reads as a rule for more than this product, the sources line also says `may belong to the team book`, so a person can move the page. An answer that explains one element becomes a line in that service's decision.
